concepts.name: Beginning, middle and end
concepts.summary: Recall that a story moves through a setup, a developing middle and a conclusion, and identify these parts in a simple tale.

concepts.name: Character and desire
concepts.summary: Explain that a story centers on a character who wants something, and that this desire drives what happens.

concepts.name: Conflict as obstacle
concepts.summary: Understand that conflict is whatever stands between the character and their goal, and that without it there is no story.

concepts.name: Stakes
concepts.summary: Explain that stakes are what the character stands to gain or lose, and that they give the audience a reason to care.

concepts.name: Climax and resolution
concepts.summary: Identify the climax as the peak moment of confrontation and the resolution as the outcome that settles the story.

concepts.name: Story versus list of events
concepts.summary: Distinguish a story, where events cause one another, from a mere sequence of things that happened.

misconceptions.text: A story is just a series of events told in order.
Conflict means a fight or violence between characters.
Stakes only matter in life-or-death stories.

concepts.name: Three-act structure
concepts.summary: Apply the setup, confrontation and resolution framework to outline a short story with turning points between acts.

concepts.name: Inciting incident
concepts.summary: Place an event early in a story that disrupts the status quo and sets the protagonist on a path toward a goal.

concepts.name: Rising action and escalation
concepts.summary: Sequence complications so each raises difficulty or stakes and builds toward the climax.

concepts.name: Story hooks
concepts.summary: Write an opening that raises a question or tension so the audience wants to hear more.

concepts.name: Basic character arc
concepts.summary: Describe how a character begins with a flaw or belief and changes by the end because of what they experience.

concepts.name: Sensory and specific detail
concepts.summary: Use specific sensory details in place of generalities to make scenes tangible.

concepts.name: Show, don't tell
concepts.summary: Rewrite abstract statements of emotion or trait into concrete actions, details and dialogue.

misconceptions.text: The inciting incident is the same as the climax.
Showing means adding more description and adjectives.
Three-act structure is a rigid formula where each act has the same length.

concepts.name: Hero's journey stages
concepts.summary: Map a story onto the stages of departure, initiation and return, such as the call, ordeal and return with the elixir.

concepts.name: Internal versus external conflict
concepts.summary: Analyse how a character's external goal and inner flaw interact, and how the want diverges from the need.

concepts.name: Business story structure
concepts.summary: Build a short business story with a relatable protagonist, a clear challenge, a turning point and a point tied to the message.

concepts.name: Audience-centered framing
concepts.summary: Analyse what an audience cares about and choose the story, details and emphasis that connect to it.

concepts.name: Turning points and reversals
concepts.summary: Identify and design moments where circumstances or understanding shift and change the story's direction.

concepts.name: Pacing and tension control
concepts.summary: Analyse how scene length, reveals and withheld information raise or release tension across a story.

concepts.name: Emotional beats
concepts.summary: Plan the sequence of emotions the audience should feel and attach each to a specific moment.

misconceptions.text: The hero's journey must be followed step by step for every story to work.
A business story just needs facts and results; emotion is unprofessional.
What the character wants and what they need are the same thing.

concepts.name: Subtext and implication
concepts.summary: Analyse how meaning conveyed through gaps, gestures and omissions engages the audience more than explicit statement.

concepts.name: Evaluating structural fit
concepts.summary: Judge which structure, such as three acts, journey, in medias res or nested stories, best suits a given purpose and context.

concepts.name: Character arc variants
concepts.summary: Distinguish positive, negative and flat arcs and analyse how each shapes theme and audience response.

concepts.name: Theme and controlling idea
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether every scene and detail serves a single underlying idea the story proves through its outcome.

concepts.name: Persuasive narrative design
concepts.summary: Evaluate how stories shift beliefs or decisions, including transportation, identification and the risk of manipulation.

concepts.name: Critique and revision
concepts.summary: Diagnose weaknesses such as flat stakes or unearned endings and revise by cutting, reordering and sharpening.

concepts.name: Oral delivery and presence
concepts.summary: Analyse how voice, pause, pacing and gesture shape the impact of a story told live.

misconceptions.text: Characters should always change positively by the end of a story.
Subtext means hiding the point so the audience has to guess it.
A moving story persuades on its own, so supporting evidence is unnecessary.

concepts.name: Original structure design
concepts.summary: Create new or hybrid narrative structures, such as nonlinear, braided or fragmented forms, that serve a specific emotional effect.

concepts.name: Subverting conventions deliberately
concepts.summary: Evaluate when breaking an expected convention strengthens a story and when it merely confuses the audience.

concepts.name: Narrative strategy for organizations
concepts.summary: Design a body of stories that carries an organization's purpose, values and change agenda across audiences and channels.

concepts.name: Ethics of storytelling
concepts.summary: Evaluate questions of truthfulness, consent, representation and emotional manipulation in using real people's stories.

concepts.name: Adapting across media
concepts.summary: Redesign one story for speech, page, screen, slides or interactive formats, using each medium's strengths.

concepts.name: Unreliable narration and perspective
concepts.summary: Evaluate how narrator choice, reliability and withheld perspective shape audience trust and interpretation.

concepts.name: Coaching others' stories
concepts.summary: Develop methods to elicit, shape and give feedback on others' stories while preserving their authentic voice.

misconceptions.text: Expert storytellers simply ignore structure and rely on instinct.
A story that is emotionally true can be freely embellished for effect.
A story that works in one medium will work unchanged in another.
